notes: Base 1.5 kg = Schneider teardown benchmark (E02, E37; Schneider-provided, masses inferred by the teardown). Range = comparable RMUs: 0.72 kg for the 12 kV reference RMU of the EU study (E11) to 2.5 kg for Siemens 8DJH (E37).
Pessimistic AR4 (legacy reporting), base AR5 (US EPA GHGRP), optimistic AR6 (GHG Protocol recommends). Old 25,200 was an AR6 draft value (E07).
Pessimistic = IEC design value for sealed systems (new units may be lower); base = IPCC Europe default incl. failures and maintenance; optimistic = IPCC Japan default.
Longer life LOWERS AirSeT's value (end-of-life and regulation costs are discounted further), so pessimistic = 60, optimistic = 30.

Customer's nominal cost of capital (Damodaran, US, Jan 2026): pessimistic = Software (Internet) 10.66 % (hyperscalers), base = US total market 6.96 %, optimistic = R.E.I.T. 5.32 % (colocation operators are REITs). A higher rate lowers AirSeT's future savings.

Pessimistic = ~1 h extra work at decommissioning, EUR 35 (producers, E11); base = Oeko-Recherche end-of-life cost EUR 2/yr per panel over a 40-year life = EUR 80 (E11); optimistic = Eaton's ~EUR 1,000 (competitor claim, E12).
EU estimates, where end-of-life rules exist; outside the EU losses are likely at least as high. E17: Schneider take-back recovers >=99 %.

Price a customer puts on its own emissions. Pessimistic = Microsoft's internal fee on operations US$15 (E75), the only data-centre operator that discloses one (E76); base = CDP median internal price US$25 (E56); optimistic = US EPA social cost of CO2 US$190 (E58), the upper reference. Converted at 1.120 US$/EUR (E59). The EU ETS (~EUR 75) is not used: it is a compliance price, not a non-EU customer's internal price.

Every adopted SF6 rule (EU, California, New York, Massachusetts) applies to new equipment or to emissions; repairs, spare parts and extensions of installed units stay allowed, and a sealed RMU needs no SF6 refilling (E09), so the 2035 EU servicing rule costs it nothing. Cost to an installed RM6 = EUR 0 in every scenario. The 'future-proof' argument is about new purchases, not the installed unit.

AirSeT premium proxied by Eaton (2025 benchmark P50, E36): pessimistic = vs the average SF6 brand +27 %; base = vs Schneider RM6 +21.98 %, the exact 2025 gap of EUR 1,921 (E01); optimistic = vs Siemens, the closest-priced SF6 rival, +3 %. Low-cost SF6 brands are +50 % (worse than pessimistic).

Installation cost difference. Schneider says RM AirSeT keeps the SF6 unit's footprint and installation practice (E171, E132), so 0 in every scenario. Risk not priced: generic SF6-free 11 kV RMUs are 20-30 % larger by volume (E168); no EUR value per m3 of data-centre electrical room was found.

Routine maintenance difference. Both are sealed for life (RM6: E170; AirSeT 'maintenance-free': E117) and manufacturers agree sealed-for-life SF6 and clean-air units have equivalent OPEX (E167), so 0. The 15-20 % OPEX saving claimed where gas handling is eliminated is captured by sf6_admin_cost_eur_per_year and the end-of-life terms, not here.

SF6-specific upkeep of an RM6 that AirSeT avoids: leak checks, gas-pressure reading, inventory and records. Pessimistic and base 0: no target market requires it (status 0-1), and EU rules exempt sealed units tested below 0.1 %/yr (E169). Optimistic EUR 50 = 1 hour a year at Eaton's EUR 50/h EU labour rate (E12) where an inventory / reporting rule applies, e.g. New York Part 495 (E64). Certified-technician training (GBP 795, E172, Low) sits in the service contractor's rate, not counted separately.
